entries.note: “Genuinely cool” does not mean “genuinely useful.” The claimed quality is expressed as subjective praise.

entries.test: Public scaling studies comparing graphical quality and compositional accuracy would test whether increased scale improves some capabilities while leaving persistent limitations.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give the limitation a concrete reading. This concerns the effects of scaling.

entries.test: Public part-whole evaluations of subsequent image generators relying on statistical learning would test the reported prediction of persistent difficulties.
entries.note: Marcus endorses his own earlier prediction. The normalization changes that historical prediction into a present-tense observation.

entries.test: Public compositionality evaluations and reproducible prompt outputs from image models available at publication, including Nano Banana, would establish their failure rates.
entries.note: “Latest” refers to models available when the post was published.

entries.test: Dated public compositionality tests from earlier and contemporary image models would show whether the same problems persisted.
entries.note: Marcus explicitly adopts the persistence claim, even though he also credits Tang.

entries.test: Public evaluations across successive model generations would compare gains in visual quality with gains in physical and compositional correctness over the years preceding publication.
entries.note: “A lot” and “much less” strengthen the original comparison, which says only “better and better” and “less so.”

entries.test: A publicly released chronological session record showing Marcus's first Nano Banana prompt and its erroneous output would establish the claim.
entries.note: An isolated failed output establishes failure but does not establish that it was his first attempt.

entries.test: Matched public bicycle and related mechanical drawing tests would compare Nano Banana and ChatGPT-5 on part-whole correctness.
entries.note: The bicycle context supplies a plain reading of “this sort of thing.”

entries.test: Public outputs and comparative evaluations of the referenced models on part-whole drawing tasks would establish whether all perform poorly.
entries.note: In context, the insult also makes a concrete claim about performance on the illustrated tasks.

entries.test: Public ChatGPT image outputs on basic anatomical and part-count prompts would show whether it continued to make elementary biological errors at publication.
entries.note: The surrounding rabbit-ear example gives “basic facts of life” a concrete biological reading.

entries.test: Public controlled scaling studies would show whether increasing scale improves visual quality while failing to improve other capabilities such as part-whole reasoning.
entries.note: The statement attributes selective improvements to scaling, making it causal.

entries.test: Dated public model evaluations and video-generation releases would establish recurring visual-quality improvements and video capability by publication.
entries.note: This describes the capabilities of the model class, without requiring every image model to generate video.
The normalization broadens the discussion of image and video systems to generative AI generally. “Just mimicry” and “deeper understanding” lack a shared empirical dividing line.
The proverb summarizes the preceding contrast between visual polish and understanding without adding an independently testable claim.
